cards.text: Next, Jesus and His disciples come to Jericho, and now they're heading out of town with a large crowd. Sitting beside the road is a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus. He can't see a thing, but he can hear the whole crowd coming his way.

cards.question: Bartimaeus hears that it's Jesus of Nazareth passing by. He can't see Him. What does he do?

answers.text: He starts crying out to Jesus
He sends someone to bring Jesus
He waits for the crowd to pass

cards.text: He shouts, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” No hello. No small talk. Straight to the POINT.

cards.question: A blind beggar is shouting beside the road as a big crowd goes by. Many of the people tell Bartimaeus to be ___.
When the crowd tells Bartimaeus to be silent, he quiets down and waits.

cards.text: He cries out all the LOUDER: “Son of David, have mercy on me!” They told this man to hush, and he heard TURN IT UP.

cards.question: Jesus is leaving Jericho with a large crowd, and one voice keeps shouting for mercy. What does Jesus do?

answers.text: He stops and has him called over
He keeps walking and waves to him
He sends a disciple to bless him

cards.text: Jesus stops and says, “Call him.” So they call the blind man.

cards.question: The people go over to Bartimaeus. What do they tell him?

answers.text: Take courage because Jesus is calling him
Stay put because Jesus will come by later
Go home because Jesus has no time today

cards.question: When Bartimaeus hears that Jesus is calling for him, he jumps up and comes to Jesus.

cards.text: He even throws off his cloak to get there. Friend, I have hit SNOOZE on days I was excited about, and this man is out of his cloak before anybody finishes saying “Get up!”

Jesus asks him, “What do you want Me to do for you?” That's the exact question He just asked James and John, two of His disciples, and they asked to sit at His right and left in His glory (Mark 10:36-37).

cards.question: Bartimaeus calls Jesus “Rabboni” and asks Him to let him ___ again.

cards.text: No seats, no glory, just his eyes. “Go,” Jesus tells him, “your faith has healed you.”

cards.question: After Jesus tells him his faith has healed him, Bartimaeus has to wait a while for his sight to come back.
Bartimaeus can see, and Jesus just told him “Go.” Where does he go?

answers.text: He follows Jesus along the road

cards.text: Immediately he can see, and he follows Jesus along the road. The man who started out sitting beside the road ends up on it, following Jesus.

findings.problem: The statement says 'When the crowd tells Bartimaeus to be silent.' Mark 10:48 says 'Many people admonished him to be silent.' Calling it the crowd stretches 'many people' into the whole large crowd. Card 4 already uses the accurate wording 'Many of the people.'

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Card 7 has just answered that Jesus stops and has him called over. Card 8 repeats that same moment ('Jesus stops and says, “Call him.” So they call the blind man.') and adds nothing new except the wording. It is a recap with no Papa Dorin voice, so it doesn't move the passage forward.

Card 8 says Jesus stopped, said 'Call him' and they called the blind man. That setup rules out both wrong answers before the baker reads them: 'Stay put because Jesus will come by later' and 'Go home because Jesus has no time today.' Only the right answer is left standing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'He even throws off his cloak to get there' adds a purpose for throwing off the cloak. Mark 10:50 says only 'Throwing off his cloak, Bartimaeus jumped up and came to Jesus' and never gives a reason.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The first sentence ('Immediately he can see, and he follows Jesus along the road') only repeats what cards 15 and 16 just answered. Only the closing observation is new, so most of the card is a recap.
Card 12 tells Mark 10:36-37, which is outside the passage. It gives that reference inline in its text, but its 'verses' field cites only Mark 10:51.
findings.question: When a story card uses verses from outside the passage and gives their reference inline, should the card's 'verses' field also include them? Or should it cite only the passage verses, given that a range like Mark 10:36-51 would be far too wide?
